title: Stretches Over Which Qualifying Monthly Earnings Are Measured
content:
Which stretch the qualifying monthly earnings of a Keyturn Host Payout Account are measured over turns on how the account settles and on whether money has lately left it.

**Where the account is swept as each trip completes and a transfer has left it in the three months up to that day**, the trip earnings credited in the twelve months up to that day are taken and divided by twelve.

**Where the account is swept as each trip completes and no transfer has left it in that period**, the trip earnings credited in the three months up to that day are taken and divided by three.

**In every other case**, the trip earnings credited in the month up to that day are taken as they stand.

Whichever stretch is taken, the figure is rounded half to even to two decimal places.

## Points of judgement

**An account swept as each trip completes that has paid something out this quarter.** The first case governs: a full year of trip earnings is taken and spread evenly over twelve months.

**The same account with nothing paid out in the three months up to that day.** The second case governs: a quarter of trip earnings is taken and spread evenly over three months.

**An account settling on any other rhythm.** The third case governs whatever has left it, and the month up to that day is taken as it stands, with no spreading.

## On hypothetical figures

Take a hypothetical account credited with trip earnings of 12000.00 USD in the twelve months up to that day, 3600.00 USD in the three months up to that day and 900.00 USD in the month up to that day. The qualifying monthly earnings as first measured are 1000.00 USD in the first case, 1200.00 USD in the second and 900.00 USD in the third.
